## Installation and deployment

### Installing dependencies

Backends are enabled by **auto-detection** at CMake time: install only the libraries for the backends you need.

#### Ubuntu/Debian

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y \
    build-essential cmake pkg-config \
    unixodbc-dev libglib2.0-dev \
    libssl-dev libcmocka-dev

# Hive/Impala (optional)
sudo apt-get install -y libthrift-c-glib-dev thrift-compiler

# Trino/Phoenix/Pinot/Druid/BigQuery (optional)
sudo apt-get install -y libcurl4-openssl-dev libjson-glib-dev

# MySQL-wire: StarRocks/Doris/ClickHouse (optional)
sudo apt-get install -y libmariadb-dev

# Flight SQL: Dremio/InfluxDB 3 (optional; Apache Arrow APT repo, GCC 14+)
sudo apt-get install -y libarrow-flight-sql-dev
```

#### Fedora/RHEL

```bash
sudo dnf install -y \
    gcc cmake pkgconfig \
    unixODBC-devel glib2-devel \
    thrift-devel libcurl-devel \
    json-glib-devel mariadb-connector-c-devel libcmocka-devel
```

#### macOS

```bash
brew install cmake unixodbc glib thrift cmocka pkg-config curl json-glib
```

#### Windows (MSYS2/UCRT64)

```bash
pacman -S \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-cmake \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-ninja \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-pkgconf \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-glib2 \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-curl \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-json-glib \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-openssl \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-glib-networking \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-libmariadbclient \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-thrift \
    mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-cmocka
```

MSYS2 ships the thrift **compiler** but not the c_glib **runtime**. Build the portable subset once, then point pkg-config at it:

```bash
bash scripts/build-thrift-c-glib.sh "$PWD/thrift-c-glib-prefix" 0.23.0
PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$PWD/thrift-c-glib-prefix/lib/pkgconfig" \
    cmake -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
```

Hive/Impala then build on Windows (they use Argus's GIO socket transport, not thrift's POSIX sockets). `glib-networking` provides TLS for that transport; the installer bundles its module and the driver loads it automatically. Add `mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-nsis` to build the installer.

### Building

```bash
cmake -B build
cmake --build build
```

#### CMake options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `BUILD_TESTING` | ON | Build unit tests |
| `BUILD_INTEGRATION_TESTS` | OFF | Build integration tests |
| `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS` | ON | Build shared library |
| `BUILD_ADBC` | ON | Build the Arrow ADBC driver (`libargus_adbc`) |
| `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` | Release | Debug or Release |
| `ARGUS_BUILD_THRIFT_BACKENDS` | auto | Hive + Impala (thrift_c_glib) |
| `ARGUS_BUILD_TRINO` / `_PHOENIX` / `_PINOT` / `_DRUID` / `_BIGQUERY` | auto | HTTP/JSON backends (libcurl + json-glib) |
| `ARGUS_BUILD_MYSQL` | auto | MySQL-wire backend (libmariadb) |
| `ARGUS_BUILD_FLIGHTSQL` | auto | Arrow Flight SQL backend (C++) |
| `ARGUS_BUILD_KUDU` | auto | Kudu backend (deprecated) |

The `ARGUS_BUILD_*` options default to whatever the dependency detection finds; the CMake output lists which backends are enabled.

#### Debug build

```bash
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
```

### Running tests

#### Unit tests

```bash
cd build
ctest --output-on-failure -L unit
```

#### Integration tests

```bash
docker compose -f tests/integration/docker-compose.yml up -d
ctest -L integration --output-on-failure
docker compose -f tests/integration/docker-compose.yml down
```

### Installation

#### Linux — .deb package

Tagged releases attach a `.deb` to [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/argus/releases). Its runtime dependencies are derived automatically from the built library (`dpkg-shlibdeps`), so `apt install ./argus-odbc_*.deb` pulls what the enabled backends need. The package registers the driver with unixODBC.

#### Linux/macOS — from source

```bash
cd build && sudo make install
```

Installs `libargus_odbc.so` (and `libargus_adbc.so` when `BUILD_ADBC` is on) to `<prefix>/lib/` and headers to `<prefix>/include/argus/`.

:::note unixODBC
Using the driver through the unixODBC Driver Manager (isql, BI tools) requires **v0.5.8 or later** — earlier builds failed with `IM005` under the DM. See [Troubleshooting](./troubleshooting.md).
:::

#### Windows

Use the NSIS installer from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/argus/releases) (or build it: `makensis installer/argus-odbc.nsi`). It registers `Argus ODBC Driver`, bundles the dependency DLLs and the glib-networking TLS module, and ships **eight backends**: Hive, Impala, Trino, Phoenix, Pinot, Druid, BigQuery and MySQL-wire. Flight SQL and Kudu need dependencies MSYS2 does not provide.

For fleet deployment, see [Deploying with Microsoft Intune](./intune-deployment.md).

### BI connectors

Tagged releases also attach the **Power BI connector** (`Argus.mez`, plus a signed `Argus.pqx` when a certificate is configured) and the **Tableau connectors** (`argus-*.taco`). They sit on top of the installed driver — install the driver first. See [BI tools](./bi-tools.md).

### Verifying

```bash
nm -D build/libargus_odbc.so | grep SQL
```

Should show `SQLAllocHandle`, `SQLConnect`, `SQLDriverConnect`, `SQLExecDirect`, etc.

---

## Deploying with Microsoft Intune

Argus can be deployed at scale on Windows endpoints using Microsoft Intune as a **Win32 app**. The driver is packaged as an `.intunewin` archive containing a signed NSIS installer and PowerShell lifecycle scripts.

### Prerequisites

- Microsoft Intune administrator access ([Intune admin center](https://intune.microsoft.com))
- [Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool](https://github.com/microsoft/Microsoft-Win32-Content-Prep-Tool) (`IntuneWinAppUtil.exe`) if you are packaging manually
- The signed `argus-odbc-installer.exe` (built via `makensis installer/argus-odbc.nsi`)
- Target devices: Windows 10 64-bit or later

:::tip Automated builds
The CI pipeline (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) generates the `.intunewin` package automatically on tagged releases and uploads it to GitHub Releases. You can skip the manual packaging step and download the artifact directly.
:::

### Packaging the .intunewin file

If you are packaging manually, stage the installer alongside the PowerShell scripts and run the content prep tool:

```powershell
# Create a staging directory
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path installer\staging -Force

# Copy artifacts
Copy-Item build\argus-odbc-installer.exe installer\staging\
Copy-Item installer\intune\Install.ps1   installer\staging\
Copy-Item installer\intune\Detect.ps1    installer\staging\
Copy-Item installer\intune\Uninstall.ps1 installer\staging\

# Generate the .intunewin package
IntuneWinAppUtil.exe `
    -c installer\staging `
    -s argus-odbc-installer.exe `
    -o installer\output
```

The output file `installer\output\argus-odbc-installer.intunewin` is ready for upload to Intune.

### Configuring the app in Intune

#### 1. Create a new Win32 app

In the [Intune admin center](https://intune.microsoft.com), navigate to **Apps > Windows > Add** and select **Windows app (Win32)**.

Upload `argus-odbc-installer.intunewin` as the app package file.

#### 2. App information

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Name** | Argus ODBC Driver |
| **Description** | Universal ODBC driver for Hive, Impala, Trino, Phoenix, Pinot, Druid, BigQuery and MySQL-wire engines (StarRocks/Doris/ClickHouse) |
| **Publisher** | Varga Foundation |
| **App version** | Match the release version (e.g. `0.5.9`) |
| **Category** | Business / Productivity |

#### 3. Program settings

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Install command** | `powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Install.ps1` |
| **Uninstall command** | `powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Uninstall.ps1` |
| **Install behavior** | **System** |
| **Device restart behavior** | No specific action |

The install runs under the SYSTEM account with administrator privileges, which is required for ODBC driver registration in `HKLM`.

#### 4. Requirements

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Operating system architecture** | 64-bit |
| **Minimum operating system** | Windows 10 1607 |

#### 5. Detection rules

Select **Use a custom detection script** and upload `Detect.ps1`.

The detection script checks two conditions:
1. The registry key `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ODBC\ODBCINST.INI\Argus ODBC Driver` exists
2. The `Driver` value points to an existing `argus_odbc.dll` file on disk

If both conditions are met, the script writes to stdout and exits `0` (detected). Otherwise it exits silently with `0` (not detected).

#### 6. Return codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Failed |
| `3010` | Soft reboot required |

#### 7. Assignments

Assign the app to the appropriate **device groups** or **user groups**. Use:
- **Required** for mandatory deployments across the organization
- **Available for enrolled devices** to let users install on demand from the Company Portal

### What the installer does

The NSIS installer (`argus-odbc-installer.exe /S`) performs the following in silent mode:

1. Copies `argus_odbc.dll` and bundled dependencies to `C:\Program Files\Argus ODBC Driver\`
2. Registers the ODBC driver in the 64-bit registry:
   ```
   HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ODBC\ODBCINST.INI\Argus ODBC Driver
       Driver      = C:\Program Files\Argus ODBC Driver\argus_odbc.dll
       Setup       = C:\Program Files\Argus ODBC Driver\argus_odbc.dll
       Description = Argus ODBC Driver
       CompanyName = Varga Foundation
       UsageCount  = 1
   ```
3. Adds the driver to `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ODBC\ODBCINST.INI\ODBC Drivers`
4. Creates Start Menu shortcuts (ODBC Data Source Administrator, Uninstaller)
5. Registers in Add/Remove Programs for standard uninstallation
6. Stores the install directory in `HKLM:\Software\Argus ODBC Driver\InstallDir`

### Testing locally

Before uploading to Intune, validate the scripts on a test machine:

```powershell
# Install
powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File installer\intune\Install.ps1

# Verify driver appears in ODBC Data Source Administrator
odbcad32.exe

# Detect (should print "Argus ODBC Driver detected")
powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File installer\intune\Detect.ps1

# Uninstall
powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File installer\intune\Uninstall.ps1
```

### Post-deployment DSN configuration

Once the driver is installed on endpoints, DSNs can be configured in several ways:

#### Via Group Policy (registry preferences)

Push a System DSN to all target machines via GPO registry preferences targeting:

```
HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ODBC\ODBC.INI\<DSN Name>
    Driver   = Argus ODBC Driver
    HOST     = <backend-host>
    PORT     = <backend-port>
    BACKEND  = <hive|impala|trino|phoenix|pinot|druid|bigquery|mysql>
    DATABASE = <default-database>
```

> Do **not** push `UID`/`PWD` through DSN properties — the Windows ODBC Manager rejects them. Supply credentials at connect time or via a DSN-less connection string.

And add the DSN name to:

```
HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ODBC\ODBC.INI\ODBC Data Sources
    <DSN Name> = Argus ODBC Driver
```

#### Via PowerShell remediation script

Deploy a [Proactive Remediation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/intune/fundamentals/remediations) script through Intune to configure DSNs programmatically:

```powershell
# Example: create a system DSN for Trino
$dsnName = "Trino Production"
$dsnPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ODBC\ODBC.INI\$dsnName"

New-Item -Path $dsnPath -Force | Out-Null
Set-ItemProperty -Path $dsnPath -Name "Driver"   -Value "C:\Program Files\Argus ODBC Driver\argus_odbc.dll"
Set-ItemProperty -Path $dsnPath -Name "HOST"      -Value "trino.example.com"
Set-ItemProperty -Path $dsnPath -Name "PORT"      -Value "8443"
Set-ItemProperty -Path $dsnPath -Name "BACKEND"   -Value "trino"
Set-ItemProperty -Path $dsnPath -Name "DATABASE"  -Value "analytics"
Set-ItemProperty -Path $dsnPath -Name "SSL"       -Value "1"

# Register the DSN
$dsPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\ODBC\ODBC.INI\ODBC Data Sources"
Set-ItemProperty -Path $dsPath -Name $dsnName -Value "Argus ODBC Driver"
```

### Monitoring deployment

Track the rollout in the Intune admin center under **Apps > Monitor > App install status**. Devices will report one of:

- **Installed** — Detection script confirmed the driver is present
- **Failed** — Install script returned exit code `1`
- **Pending** — Waiting for device check-in
- **Not applicable** — Device does not meet requirements (e.g. 32-bit OS)

For troubleshooting failed deployments on a device, check the Intune Management Extension logs:

```
C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs\IntuneManagementExtension.log
```

### Updating the driver

To push a new version:

1. Build and package the new `.intunewin` file
2. In the Intune admin center, edit the existing **Argus ODBC Driver** app
3. Upload the new package file under **App package file**
4. Update the **App version** field
5. Save — Intune will reinstall on devices where the detection script no longer matches

The NSIS installer overwrites the previous DLL in-place, so no separate uninstall step is needed for upgrades.

### Deploying the Power BI connector alongside

If your fleet uses Power BI Desktop with the [Argus custom connector](./bi-tools.md#power-bi), deploy it with the driver:

1. Distribute the signed `Argus.pqx` to `%USERPROFILE%\Documents\Power BI Desktop\Custom Connectors\` (e.g. via an Intune PowerShell script or a second Win32 app).
2. Push its certificate thumbprint to the `REG_MULTI_SZ` value `TrustedCertificateThumbprints` under `HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Power BI Desktop` via GPO or Intune policy — Power BI then loads the signed connector at the *Recommended* security level with no per-user toggle.

---

## Operations

### Logging

Enable logging via connection string or environment variables:

```
LogLevel=5;LogFile=/var/log/argus.log
```

Or:

```bash
export ARGUS_LOG_LEVEL=5
export ARGUS_LOG_FILE=/var/log/argus.log
```

#### Log levels

| Level | Name | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| 0 | OFF | No logging |
| 1 | FATAL | Fatal errors only |
| 2 | ERROR | Errors |
| 3 | WARN | Warnings |
| 4 | INFO | Informational messages |
| 5 | DEBUG | Debug details |
| 6 | TRACE | Full trace (verbose) |

Logging is thread-safe with mutex-protected operations on all platforms.

### Timeouts

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| ConnectTimeout | Maximum time to establish a connection |
| QueryTimeout | Maximum time for a query to complete |
| SocketTimeout | Maximum time for socket read/write |

```
ConnectTimeout=30;QueryTimeout=600;SocketTimeout=120
```

### Connection retry

Automatic retry on connection failure:

```
RetryCount=3;RetryDelay=2
```

Diagnostics are cleared between attempts. Each attempt is logged.

### Query cancellation

Cancel long-running queries from another thread:

```c
SQLCancel(stmt);
```

`SQLCancel` is dispatched to the backend, which sends the engine's own cancellation request — e.g.:

- **Trino**: DELETE `/v1/query/{id}`
- **Hive/Impala**: `TCancelOperationReq` via Thrift
- **Phoenix**: Avatica `closeStatement` RPC
- **Kudu**: Closes the `KuduScanner` immediately

### Fetch tuning

Adjust `FetchBufferSize` to control memory usage and network round trips:

```
FetchBufferSize=5000
```

Default is 1000 rows per batch. Increase for large result sets, decrease for low-latency queries.

For array-oriented applications, use **block fetch** (`SQL_ATTR_ROW_ARRAY_SIZE` + `SQLFetchScroll`) to retrieve rowsets in one call, and `SQL_ATTR_PARAMSET_SIZE` for parameter arrays. Static scrollable cursors (`SQLFetchScroll` PRIOR/FIRST/LAST/ABSOLUTE/RELATIVE) are supported.

The Flight SQL backend streams Arrow record batches lazily — one block per fetch — so memory stays bounded regardless of result size.

### Monitoring

- Monitor log files for connection errors and query failures.
- Use `ApplicationName` to track queries in backend UIs (Trino UI, HiveServer2 logs).
- Track connection retry events at WARN level.

### Upgrades

- Linux: install the new `.deb` (or replace `libargus_odbc.so` for source builds). Windows: run the new installer — it overwrites in place.
- No schema migrations needed (stateless driver).
- Update DSN configuration if new parameters are available.
- If you deploy the [Power BI or Tableau connectors](./bi-tools.md), they version independently of the driver — an upgraded driver keeps working with an older connector and vice versa, but ship both from the same release when you can.

---

## Prerequisites and resources

### Build prerequisites

- CMake 3.16+
- C compiler (GCC, Clang, or MinGW)
- C++ compiler (only for the Flight SQL and Kudu backends; Flight SQL needs GCC 14+ / C++20)
- pkg-config

### Library dependencies

| Library | Purpose | Required |
|---------|---------|----------|
| unixODBC | ODBC driver manager (Linux/macOS) | Yes |
| GLib 2.0 / GIO 2.0 | Core utilities, socket transport and timeouts | Yes |
| Thrift C GLib | Hive/Impala backends | Optional |
| libcurl | Trino/Phoenix/Pinot/Druid/BigQuery backends | Optional |
| json-glib | Trino/Phoenix/Pinot/Druid/BigQuery backends | Optional |
| libmariadb | MySQL-wire backend (StarRocks/Doris/ClickHouse) | Optional |
| arrow-flight-sql (C++) | Flight SQL backend (Dremio/InfluxDB 3) | Optional |
| libkudu_client | Kudu backend (deprecated) | Optional |
| OpenSSL | SSL/TLS for Thrift; BigQuery service-account keys (RS256) | Optional |
| GSSAPI (system) | Kerberos for Hive/Impala on Linux/macOS (SSPI is used on Windows) | Optional |
| glib-networking | TLS module for the GIO transport on Windows (bundled by the installer) | Optional |
| cmocka | Unit tests | Optional |

Backends are enabled by **auto-detection** of these dependencies at CMake time — you only need the libraries for the backends you plan to use.

### Backend prerequisites

#### Apache Hive (also Spark / Flink / Databricks)
- HiveServer2 accessible on port 10000 (default), Thrift binary protocol — or HTTP transport (`TransportMode=HTTP`)
- Spark Thrift Server and Flink SQL Gateway (`hiveserver2` endpoint) speak the same protocol: use `BACKEND=hive`

#### Apache Impala
- Impala daemon accessible on port 21050 (default)
- Thrift binary protocol enabled

#### Trino
- Trino coordinator accessible on port 8080 (default)
- REST API enabled (default)

#### Apache Phoenix
- Phoenix Query Server (PQS) accessible on port 8765 (default)
- PQS must be running with the Avatica JSON serialization (default)
- HBase cluster accessible from PQS

#### Apache Pinot
- Pinot broker accessible on port 8000 (default) for queries
- Pinot controller accessible on port 9000 (same host) for table listing

#### Apache Druid
- Druid router (port 8888) or broker (port 8082) accessible
- SQL endpoint (`/druid/v2/sql`) enabled (default)

#### Google BigQuery
- A GCP project id (`Project=`)
- A service-account JSON key (`BQKeyFile=`), a pre-fetched token (`AccessToken=`), or an unauthenticated emulator endpoint
- For sovereign clouds: the deployment's API/token endpoints and its CA certificate

#### MySQL-wire (StarRocks / Doris / ClickHouse)
- The engine's MySQL protocol port: StarRocks/Doris FE `9030`, ClickHouse `9004`, MySQL/MariaDB `3306`

#### Arrow Flight SQL (Dremio / InfluxDB 3)
- A Flight SQL endpoint: Dremio `32010` (default), InfluxDB 3 `8181`
- A build with `libarrow-flight-sql-dev` (Apache Arrow APT repo)

#### Apache Kudu (deprecated)
- Prefer reaching Kudu tables through Impala (`BACKEND=impala`)
- If used directly: Kudu master on port 7051 and `libkudu_client` installed — note it is **not packaged for any Ubuntu newer than 16.04**

### Resources

- CPU: Minimal, driver runs in the client application process
- Memory: Proportional to `FetchBufferSize` (default 1000 rows per batch); Flight SQL streams record batches lazily with bounded memory
- Disk: Minimal, only needed for optional log files

---

## Security

### SSL/TLS

Argus supports SSL/TLS for all backends. Enable via the connection string:

```
SSL=1;SSLCAFile=/etc/ssl/certs/ca.pem;SSLVerify=1
```

#### Trino / Phoenix / Pinot / Druid

- Full HTTPS with certificate verification (libcurl)
- Client certificate and key support (mutual TLS)

```
HOST=trino.example.com;PORT=8443;
SSL=1;SSLVerify=1;
SSLCertFile=/opt/certs/client-cert.pem;
SSLKeyFile=/opt/certs/client-key.pem;
SSLCAFile=/opt/certs/root-ca.pem;
BACKEND=trino
```

#### Hive/Impala

- TLS on the Thrift transport, with CA certificate configuration
- On Windows the GIO transport uses the bundled `glib-networking` TLS module — loaded automatically by the driver

```
HOST=hive.example.com;PORT=10000;
SSL=1;SSLCAFile=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt;SSLVerify=1;
BACKEND=hive
```

#### BigQuery

- HTTPS to the API and token endpoints; `SSLCAFile` is honoured for **both** — required for sovereign clouds whose private PKI is not in the system trust store
- Mutual TLS via `SSLCertFile`/`SSLKeyFile`

#### MySQL-wire

- TLS via libmariadb: `SSL=1` with `SSLCertFile`/`SSLKeyFile`/`SSLCAFile`, `SSLVerify` honored

#### Flight SQL

- `SSL=1` uses a TLS gRPC channel

### Authentication

Set via the `AUTHMECH` connection string parameter (see the [full table](./configuration.md#authentication-mechanisms)).

#### Username / password

- **Hive/Impala**: `PLAIN`/`LDAP` — SASL PLAIN negotiated during Thrift session open.
- **Trino**: `LDAP`/`PLAIN`/`BASIC` (or simply supplying `PWD`) — HTTP Basic; **requires TLS** (`SSL=1`).
- **Pinot/Druid**: optional HTTP Basic via `UID`/`PWD`.
- **MySQL-wire**: native MySQL authentication.
- **Flight SQL**: `UID`+`PWD` → Flight handshake (basic token).

#### Kerberos

`AuthMech=KERBEROS` (alias `GSSAPI`) for Hive, Impala and Trino:

- **Linux/macOS**: system GSSAPI — a `kinit` ticket or keytab.
- **Windows**: **native SSPI** using the logged-in domain user's credentials — no MIT Kerberos install required.
- **Trino** and Hive over HTTP transport use SPNEGO/Negotiate via libcurl.

The service principal defaults to `hive/<host>` (`impala/<host>` for Impala), with the realm resolved from the Kerberos config. Override with:

- `KrbServiceName` — the SPN service (default `hive`/`impala`).
- `KrbHostFQDN` — the SPN host, when it differs from the connection `HOST` (load balancer, connection by IP).
- `KrbRealm` — an explicit realm, producing `service/host@REALM` (cross-realm, or no `domain_realm` mapping).

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=hive;HOST=hive.example.com;PORT=10000;AuthMech=KERBEROS;KrbServiceName=hive
```

#### Bearer tokens (JWT / Databricks)

`AuthMech=JWT` (aliases `BEARER`, `DATABRICKS`, `TOKEN`) sends the token in `PWD` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`:

- **Trino**: any JWT-gated cluster.
- **Hive over HTTP** (`TransportMode=HTTP`): Databricks SQL warehouses (personal access tokens), or any token-gated HiveServer2/Spark endpoint (e.g. behind Apache Knox).

#### OAuth2 (Trino)

- **`OAUTH2` / `CLIENT_CREDENTIALS`** — machine-to-machine: Argus fetches a token from the IdP token endpoint and uses it as the bearer. Params: `OAuth2TokenEndpoint`, `ClientId`, `ClientSecret`, optional `Scope`. The token is **re-fetched automatically** on `401` (expiry) and the request retried transparently.
- **`DEVICE_CODE`** — device authorization grant (RFC 8628) for headless/no-browser logins: Argus prints the verification URL and user code, polls the token endpoint until authorized. Params: `OAuth2DeviceEndpoint`, `OAuth2TokenEndpoint`, `ClientId`, optional `Scope`.
- **`AUTH_CODE` / `BROWSER` / `SSO`** — authorization-code grant with PKCE and a browser + loopback redirect (the standard interactive cloud-BI flow): Argus opens the system browser (honoring `$BROWSER`), listens on `127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>`, exchanges the code at the token endpoint. Params: `OAuth2AuthEndpoint`, `OAuth2TokenEndpoint`, `ClientId`, optional `ClientSecret`/`Scope`.
- **OIDC discovery** — instead of giving each endpoint, set `OAuth2Issuer` and Argus fetches `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` to discover them. Works with all three flows.

```
DRIVER=Argus;BACKEND=trino;HOST=trino;PORT=8443;SSL=1;AuthMech=OAUTH2;OAuth2Issuer=https://idp.example.com;ClientId=cid;ClientSecret=csec;Scope=trino
```

#### BigQuery service accounts

`BQKeyFile` points at a service-account JSON key; Argus performs the RS256 JWT-bearer grant against the (configurable) token endpoint. Alternatively, `AccessToken` supplies a pre-fetched bearer token. See [Configuration](./configuration.md#google-bigquery-backendbigquery).

### Query tracking

Use `ApplicationName` to identify queries in backend audit logs:

- **Trino**: Sets `X-Trino-Source` HTTP header
- **Hive**: Sets `hive.query.source` session configuration
- **Phoenix**: Sent in Avatica connection properties

```
ApplicationName=MyETLPipeline
```

### Best practices

- Use SSL/TLS in production (`SSL=1;SSLVerify=1`).
- Use absolute paths for certificate and key files.
- Never leave `SSLVerify=0` outside a test bench.
- Prefer Kerberos or OAuth2 to static passwords where the cluster supports them.
- Never put `PWD` (passwords or tokens) in a world-readable DSN file; on Windows the ODBC Manager refuses `UID`/`PWD` in DSN properties — supply them at connect time.
- Rotate certificates, tokens and service-account keys on a regular schedule.
- Use `ApplicationName` for audit trail.

---

## Troubleshooting

### Common issues

#### Connection fails

- Enable trace logging: `LogLevel=6;LogFile=/tmp/argus.log`
- Check firewall rules and network reachability.
- Verify `HOST`, `PORT`, and `BACKEND` values.
- Try retry: `RetryCount=3;RetryDelay=2`

#### unixODBC reports IM005 ("Driver's SQLAllocHandle failed")

Fixed in **v0.5.8** — earlier versions failed under the unixODBC Driver Manager (which blocked isql and every Linux BI tool). Upgrade the driver; there is no workaround for older builds.

#### SSL errors

- Verify certificate paths are absolute and readable.
- Check certificate validity and expiration.
- Try `SSLVerify=0` for testing (never in production).
- Ensure the backend has SSL/TLS enabled on its side.
- BigQuery on a sovereign cloud: `SSLCAFile` must carry the deployment's private CA — it is used for both the API and the token endpoint.

#### Query hangs

- Set a timeout: `QueryTimeout=300`
- Use `SQLCancel` from another thread.
- Check backend logs for stuck queries.

#### Wrong backend selected

- Verify the `BACKEND` parameter is set (`hive`, `impala`, `trino`, `phoenix`, `pinot`, `druid`, `bigquery`, `mysql`, `flightsql`, or `kudu`).
- Default is `hive` if not specified.

#### Type conversion errors

- Check the source column type against the bound C type.
- Enable DEBUG logging to see conversion details.
- Complex types (ARRAY, MAP, STRUCT) are returned as JSON strings.
- ISO-8601 timestamps with a `T` separator (e.g. from Druid) are accepted since v0.5.8.

#### Driver not found

- Verify `/etc/odbcinst.ini` has an `[Argus]` section.
- Check the `Driver` path points to the actual `libargus_odbc.so` location.
- Run `odbcinst -q -d` to list registered drivers.

#### isql returns "Data source name not found"

- Verify `/etc/odbc.ini` or `~/.odbc.ini` has the DSN defined.
- Run `odbcinst -q -s` to list registered DSNs.

### BI tool issues

#### Power BI query folding broken / quoted identifiers rejected

Fixed in **v0.5.9**: `SQL_IDENTIFIER_QUOTE_CHAR` is now dialect-aware. Earlier versions reported a backtick for every backend, which broke Power BI query folding on Trino, Phoenix, Pinot and Druid (which need the ANSI double-quote). Upgrade the driver.

#### Power BI: "Keep Top N" does not fold / no DirectQuery

Generic ODBC cannot fold `LIMIT`/`TOP` in Power Query — that is a Power Query architecture limit. Install the [Argus custom connector](./bi-tools.md#power-bi).

#### A tool's `{fn ...}` query is rejected with 42000

The backend's dialect cannot render that function, and the driver refuses to forward it (a clear driver error beats an opaque server syntax error). If the server *does* support the function, this is a dialect-table bug in the driver — please report it.

#### Windows: Add-OdbcDsn fails with UID/PWD

The Windows ODBC Manager rejects `UID`/`PWD` in DSN properties. Supply credentials at connect time or in a DSN-less connection string.

### Authentication issues

- **Kerberos (Hive/Impala)**: verify a ticket exists (`klist`; on Windows the domain logon provides it). If the SPN differs from `service/<HOST>`, set `KrbServiceName`, `KrbHostFQDN` or `KrbRealm`.
- **Trino Basic/LDAP rejected**: HTTP Basic requires TLS — set `SSL=1`.
- **Trino OAuth2 401 loops**: the token is auto-refreshed once on 401; persistent 401 means the IdP client/scope configuration is wrong. Enable `LogLevel=5` to see the token exchanges.
- **BigQuery**: check `Project` is set, and that `BQKeyFile` is readable and its service account has BigQuery permissions.

### Backend-specific issues

#### Phoenix

- **Avatica error: connection refused**: Ensure Phoenix Query Server is running on the specified host and port (default 8765).
- **Avatica error: no such connection**: The PQS connection may have timed out. Reconnect and retry.
- **Empty result sets**: Verify the Phoenix table exists and has data. Use the Phoenix `sqlline` tool to test queries directly.

#### Trino v2 spooling

- **"Unsupported spooling encoding"**: The driver only supports `json` encoding. Compressed encodings (`json+zstd`, `json+lz4`) are not yet supported. Ensure your Trino server is not forcing compressed encoding.
- **Spooled segment fetch fails**: The spooled segment URI may have expired or the coordinator may be unreachable. Check network connectivity and segment TTLs.
- **Mixed v1/v2 responses**: This is normal. Even with `TrinoProtocol=v2`, the server may return v1-format data for some responses.
- **v2 not working**: Verify Trino is 466+, `TrinoProtocol=v2` is set, and (with `LogLevel=5`) that the `X-Trino-Client-Capabilities` header is sent.

#### Pinot

- **Connection works but no tables**: table listing goes through the **controller** on port 9000 of the same host — ensure it is reachable, not just the broker.
- Query errors surface the real Pinot message in the diagnostics.

#### Druid

- **Connection refused**: point `HOST`/`PORT` at the **router** (8888) or a broker (8082), not the coordinator.
- Query errors surface Druid's `errorMessage`.

#### MySQL-wire (StarRocks / Doris / ClickHouse)

- **Connection refused**: set `PORT` explicitly — StarRocks/Doris FE listen on `9030` and ClickHouse's MySQL interface on `9004`, not 3306.
- **No schemas listed**: a database is reported as an ODBC *catalog* (`TABLE_CAT`), with the schema column empty — the MySQL Connector/ODBC convention. Look under catalogs in your tool.
- **ClickHouse rejects a function**: ClickHouse's SQL is not MySQL's; the driver already refuses the escapes that differ, but tool-generated raw SQL may still not apply. Prefer generic/DSN usage over the MySQL-dialect connectors for ClickHouse.

#### Flight SQL

- **Connection fails**: verify the Flight SQL port (Dremio 32010, InfluxDB 3 8181) and whether the server requires TLS (`SSL=1`).
- **InfluxDB 3**: pass the target database via `DATABASE` (sent as the gRPC `database` header) and the token via `PWD`.

#### Kudu (deprecated)

- Prefer `BACKEND=impala`. If using the direct backend: only basic `SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... LIMIT` parses; table and column names are case-sensitive; verify the master is reachable on 7051 and `libkudu_client` is installed.

### Debug tips

- Set `LogLevel=6` for maximum verbosity.
- Check log output for Thrift, HTTP, gRPC, or MySQL client errors.
- Use `isql -v <DSN>` to test connectivity (requires driver v0.5.8+).
- Verify the shared library exports: `nm -D libargus_odbc.so | grep SQL`

---

## Cost Guide

## Cost Management Guide

Estimating, controlling, and optimizing costs for the Azurite Ambari Management Pack on Azure.

All prices are approximate US East region pay-as-you-go rates. Actual prices vary by region, commitment, and Azure pricing changes. Check the [Azure Pricing Calculator](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/calculator/) for current rates.

---

### Cluster Cost Estimation

#### Default VM Sizes and Rates

These are the default VM sizes from the mpack configuration (azure-vm-pool-site):

| Node Type | Default VM Size | vCPUs | RAM (GB) | Approx $/hr | Approx $/month (730 hrs) |
|-----------|----------------|-------|----------|-------------|-------------------------|
| Head Node | Standard_D4_v3 | 4 | 16 | $0.192 | $140 |
| Worker Node | Standard_D4_v3 | 4 | 16 | $0.192 | $140 |
| ZooKeeper | Standard_A2_v2 | 2 | 4 | $0.091 | $66 |

#### Storage Costs

| Storage Type | Unit | Approx Rate |
|-------------|------|-------------|
| ADLS Gen2 (Hot tier) | Per GB/month | $0.018 |
| ADLS Gen2 (Cool tier) | Per GB/month | $0.010 |
| ADLS Gen2 read operations | Per 10,000 | $0.004 |
| ADLS Gen2 write operations | Per 10,000 | $0.065 |
| Premium SSD (P10, 128 GB) | Per disk/month | $19.71 |
| Standard SSD (E10, 128 GB) | Per disk/month | $9.60 |
| Standard HDD (S10, 128 GB) | Per disk/month | $5.89 |

#### Managed Disk Costs per Node

| Node Type | OS Disk | Data Disks | Monthly Disk Cost |
|-----------|---------|------------|-------------------|
| Head Node | 128 GB Premium SSD ($19.71) | 2 x 256 GB Premium SSD ($39.42) | $59.13 |
| Worker Node | 128 GB Standard HDD ($5.89) | 4 x 512 GB Standard HDD ($23.56) | $29.45 |
| ZooKeeper | 128 GB Standard SSD ($9.60) | None | $9.60 |

(D8_v3 used for medium: 8 vCPUs, 32 GB RAM, ~$0.384/hr)

#### Large Cluster (Enterprise): 50 Workers

| Component | Count | VM $/month | Disk $/month | Subtotal |
|-----------|-------|------------|-------------|----------|

| ZooKeeper nodes | 5 | $330 | $48 | $378 |
